THE MYTH OF A PERFECT TEEN SCHEDULE

In today's competitive world, teens are constantly seeking the perfect routine that balances university
applications, social life, extracurricular activities, family expectations, and eight hours of sleep. Many
turn to detailed planning as a way to solve their troubles, believing that there is one single “ideal” way
to organize their time. Their quest for this is fueled by peer pressure and competitive college
admissions. 5

However, what seems achievable in theory often ends up becoming a pressure cooker in
reality. A typical high schooler's day can stretch from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. All this time is spent with the
aim of securing a place at a good college. The first sacrifice on this path, along with many more to
come, is rest. Struggling to balance everything, deadlines, test preparation, and sports events, under
the pressure that every hour must be used "productively," teens leave little room for downtime, which 10
takes a toll on their mental and physical health.

A lot of the pressure comes from how much university entrance affects future opportunities,
yet not every teen has the same resources to follow an ideal schedule that helps to get into a good
institution. Finances, family circumstances, and heavy workloads make this goal achievable only for
some. Access to private tutoring, quiet study spaces, or extra academic programs can make a 15
significant difference, but these supports are not available to all students. Teens who have jobs or
family responsibilities are often at a disadvantage, and their struggles frequently go unrecognized.

For these underprivileged teens, failing to perform at their “best” can feel especially overwhelming,
particularly when compared to peers with more advantages.

A schedule that works effectively begins with identifying priorities, including non-negotiable 20
activities such as school, homework, family responsibilities, commutes, and meals. It also requires
paying attention to personal energy patterns, such as peak focus times and periods of fatigue, as well
as being aware of which tasks require the most mental effort. This helps to organize the schedule
efficiently by doing demanding work during high-energy hours and by leaving lighter tasks to be
completed during lower-energy periods. Extracurricular activities should be kept manageable and 25
include low-stress, enjoyable pastimes, such as music, walks, or socializing. Periods without
obligations provide rest and help prevent burnout. Teenagers have different rhythms and each
student should organize their time according to their own abilities and priorities.

Nor nori nork

Gure amak beti esaten zigun erabili ezean, euskara hil egingo zela. Gure belaunaldikoek
gure gain sentitu dugu euskararen biziraupenaren ardura, hala erakutsi zigutelako. Aurrekoan
Jon Maiak “Kantu bat gara” ikuskizun ederra eskaini zuen Gasteizen. Bertan Arabari merezitako
omenaldia egin zion eta gogoratu zuen azken hamarkadetan euskara ez dela inon Araban
beste hazi. Berotasun berezi bat sentitu genuen han izan ginen guztiok eta esango nuke
bereziki hunkitu zirela zailtasun guztien gainetik aspaldi euskara ikasi zuten arabarrek. Eta
honek pentsarazi dit duela berrogei urte euskara ikasi zutenen eta gaur egun euskara ikasten
ari direnen artean dagoen diferentziaz. Esango nuke gaur egun euskara bere testuinguru
soziologiko-politiko-historikorik gabe irakasten dela kasu askotan, hizkuntza normalizatu bat
izango balitz bezala. Eta modaz kanpo dagoen zerbait esango dut, baina iruditzen zait hain
egoera zaurgarrian dagoen hizkuntza bat ezin dela irakatsi baren biziraupenerako beharrezkoa
den militantzia eta ahalegin berezi baten beharra transmititu gabe. Hizkuntza irakastearekin
batera, irakatsi behar da euskara ez dela ingelesa, ez dela espainola, ez dela frantsesa; nahiko
genukeela haien egoera guretzat, baina ez, erabili ezean, euskara galdu egingo dugun
hizkuntza bat dela gogorarazi behar da etengabe, guri txikitatik transmititu ziguten bezala. Gaur
egun euskararen hazkundea gazteen euskalduntzetik dator batez ere: egungo euskal hiztun
gehienak, familiaren bidez baino gehiago, hezkuntza sistemaren bidez edota euskaltegien
bidez jasotzen ari dira euskara. Baina ez dugu ahaztu behar hizkuntza irakastearekin ez dela
nahikoa: euskararen ibilbidea ezagutu behar dugu euskararen erabilerak duen balioaz ohar
gaitezen. Gure ahotsik gabe euskararen kantua desagertuko dela behin eta berriz gogoraraztea
beharrezkoa da. Euskara ez dela soilik nor nori nork.

Karmele Jaio, Diario de Noticias Álava, 2025/01/04

‘Eingule?’ leiaketea jaietan

Andra Mari eta Santa Eufemia jaiak ospatuko dabes laster. Jaiok girotzeko,
Eingule? leiaketea atondu dabe. Gasteen parte-artzea sustatu guran, Udalak eta
Txosna batzordeak txosnagunea edegitten dan egunerako, iraillaren 6rako,
leiaketea prestau dabe.

Leiaketearen elburua bertoko iskerea, identidadea eta kulturea edatzea da,
eta errittarrei nortasuna emoten deutzen iskereak egunerokorako daukan balioa
agirian ixtea. Orretarako, errian erabiltten diran berba errasak berreskuratu gura
dabes.

Eingule? leiaketan parte-artzea errittar gustiei edegitta dago; banaka,
bikoteka edo taldeka parte hartu daitteke eta telefono bides olgau beharko da.
